USMLE-style practice · Pharmacology

Cumulative movement-disorder risk

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

An older woman has taken metoclopramide continuously for months for diabetic gastroparesis. She develops repetitive lip smacking and tongue protrusion. Which treatment-related factor most strongly increases the risk of this potentially persistent syndrome?

  1. A brief isolated reduction in gastric acidity
  2. Concurrent oral rehydration
  3. Low dietary sodium intake
  4. Longer duration and greater cumulative exposure
  5. A single meal taken before the first dose
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Longer duration and greater cumulative exposure

Tardive dyskinesia risk rises with duration and cumulative dose; treatment should be reassessed and stopped if signs develop.

Understanding the options

Longer duration and greater cumulative exposure
Tardive dyskinesia risk rises with duration and cumulative dose; treatment should be reassessed and stopped if signs develop.
A single meal taken before the first dose
Meal timing does not account for cumulative tardive risk.
A brief isolated reduction in gastric acidity
Acidity changes do not cause this dopamine-blockade syndrome.
Concurrent oral rehydration
Rehydration does not increase tardive risk.
Low dietary sodium intake
Sodium restriction is not the relevant determinant.
